Class LogStorage

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.telemetry.LogStorage
public final class LogStorage extends Object
Where the robot's logs go on SystemCore, and keeping them from filling its storage.

A full internal disk is a SystemCore failure other teams have hit at events: a robot that rebooted mid-match with an empty log, another that lost control with 50 MB left, deploys that deleted the robot program (wpilibsuite/SystemcoreTesting #210, #211, #156). Every log goes to internal storage when no USB stick is in, and nothing else ever deletes them; the bench unit had 408 MB of them after two days. So:

  • chooseFolder() waits briefly for a USB stick to mount before settling on internal storage: the robot program can start before /U is mounted (SystemcoreTesting #341).
  • cleanUpAtBoot() deletes the oldest logs before this boot's log exists.
  • start() checks free space off the main thread and trims the internal folder if the disk runs short; periodic() turns the result into alerts and log values on the main thread.

SystemCore can boot with its clock behind older logs, so this boot's log can sort oldest. A file is never deleted if it appeared after cleanUpAtBoot() or was modified within ACTIVE_WINDOW_MILLIS.

    • chooseFolder

      public static String chooseFolder()

      Returns:
      the log folder, created if needed

    • cleanUp

      public static long[] cleanUp(File dir, long capBytes, long freeFloorBytes, int keepNewest, Set<String> protectedNames)
      Deletes the oldest log files in dir until they total at most capBytes and the disk has at least freeFloorBytes free.
      Parameters:
      dir - the log folder
      capBytes - most the logs may total
      freeFloorBytes - free space to leave on the disk
      keepNewest - how many of the newest logs are kept
      protectedNames - files never deleted
      Returns:
      {count deleted, bytes deleted}
